_note: Translations for /wissen/zitate (src/data/zitate.json), machine drafts, not yet reviewed by native speakers. Per help language: the quote (`text`, shown behind the „Übersetzung zeigen“ button), the easy-German explanation (`meaning`, shown in the UI language automatically) and, for languages the word data lacks, `words` (3 glosses). Built by merging the per-language files; see the commit that added it.

fremde-sprachen.text: Whoever knows no foreign languages knows nothing of their own.
fremde-sprachen.meaning: When you learn a new language, you also understand your mother tongue better.

schiller-kluge-mann-baut-vor.meaning: A wise person thinks about tomorrow and gets ready. Today people say this when someone prepares, for example saves money or takes an umbrella.

vater-werden.text: Becoming a father is not hard, / being a father, though, is very hard.
vater-werden.meaning: Having a child happens quickly. Being a good father is a lot of work.

musik-irrtum.text: Without music, life would be a mistake.
musik-irrtum.meaning: Music is so important that a life without music would make no sense.

mut-verstand.text: Have the courage to use your own understanding!
mut-verstand.meaning: Think for yourself! Don't just believe what other people say.

freiheit.text: Freedom is always the freedom of those who think differently.
freiheit.meaning: Freedom does not only mean: I may say my opinion. It also means: people who think differently may say their opinion.

lichtenberg-kopf-und-buch.text: When a book and a head collide and there is a hollow sound, is it always the book?
lichtenberg-kopf-und-buch.meaning: When a book seems boring or empty, maybe the problem is not the book but the reader. A funny sentence against quick judgments.

goethe-in-der-beschraenkung.text: It is in limitation that the master first shows himself, / And only law can give us freedom.
goethe-in-der-beschraenkung.meaning: A true master can create great things even with strict rules and few means. Rules can make you free, not only unfree.

schiller-gedankenfreiheit.meaning: Marquis Posa asks the king: Let people think freely. To this day the sentence is a call for freedom of opinion.

busch-fruehe-morgenzuege.text: It's the early morning trains, of course, / That are the easiest to miss.
busch-fruehe-morgenzuege.meaning: The earlier the appointment, the easier it is to oversleep. A sentence every commuter knows.

nietzsche-ergangene-gedanken.text: Only thoughts reached by walking have value.
nietzsche-ergangene-gedanken.meaning: Good ideas come while you go for a walk, not while you sit for a long time. Nietzsche himself went walking for many hours every day.

buecher-verbrennt.text: Where they burn books, they will in the end burn people too.
buecher-verbrennt.meaning: People who burn books also have no respect for people. More than 100 years later, in 1933, the Nazis burned books – Heine's too.

modersohn-fest.text: I know I will not live very long. But is that sad? Is a party more beautiful because it is longer?
modersohn-fest.meaning: A life is not only good if it is long. What matters is how intensely and beautifully you live. She really did die at only 31.

kafka-hindernis.text: Don't spend your time searching for the obstacle; maybe there is none.
kafka-hindernis.meaning: We often look for a long time for the reason why something doesn't work. Maybe there is no reason at all, and you can just start.

goethe-hier-bin-ich-mensch.text: Here I am human, here I may be so!
goethe-hier-bin-ich-mensch.meaning: Faust goes for a walk on Easter Sunday and feels free among the people. Today people say this when they feel good and free in a place.

schiller-frueh-uebt-sich.text: Whoever wants to be a master must start practising early.
schiller-frueh-uebt-sich.meaning: If you want to be very good at something, you have to start young. People often say this with a smile when children are already good at something.

busch-was-lernen-muss.text: And so it has been resolved: / That man must learn a thing or two.
busch-was-lernen-muss.meaning: Learning is part of life, for every person. Many Germans know these two lines by heart and say them with a smile.

nichts-weiss.text: Whoever knows nothing must believe everything.
nichts-weiss.meaning: If you know nothing, you cannot check whether something is true. Learning makes you free.

nietzsche-tanzender-stern.text: I tell you: one must still have chaos within oneself to give birth to a dancing star.
nietzsche-tanzender-stern.meaning: Unrest and confusion inside us are not only bad. Something new and beautiful can grow out of them, for example art or a new idea.

kant-kategorischer-imperativ.text: Act only according to that maxim through which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
kant-kategorischer-imperativ.meaning: This is the “categorical imperative”. Before you do something, ask yourself: Would it be good if all people acted like this? If not, don't do it.

luxemburg-mildes-laecheln.text: One must take everything, in public affairs as in private life: calmly, generously and with a gentle smile.
luxemburg-mildes-laecheln.meaning: In politics and in your own life you should stay calm, not be petty, and smile kindly.

goethe-zu-sagen-wie-ich-leide.text: And when man falls silent in his agony, / A god gave me the power to say how I suffer.
goethe-zu-sagen-wie-ich-leide.meaning: Other people go silent when they suffer a lot. The poet Tasso can put his pain into words. That is his gift.

schiller-aranjuez.text: The beautiful days in Aranjuez / Are now at an end.
schiller-aranjuez.meaning: The good, easy time is over. Today people say it with humour, for example at the end of a holiday.

busch-frosch-auf-dem-baum.text: When someone who, with effort, barely / Has crawled up into a tree / Already thinks he is a bird, / He is mistaken.
busch-frosch-auf-dem-baum.meaning: A small success does not make you a master yet. If you feel big too early, you can easily fall down like the frog.

lichtenberg-geld-welt.text: In German, “Geld” (money) rhymes with “Welt” (world); there could hardly be a more sensible rhyme; I defy all other languages!
lichtenberg-geld-welt.meaning: “Geld” (money) and “Welt” (world) sound alike, and money does rule the world. Lichtenberg makes fun of this and says: No other language can beat this rhyme.

heine-alte-geschichte.text: It is an old story, / Yet it always stays new.
heine-alte-geschichte.meaning: Heine is talking about heartbreak: it is as old as humanity, but it feels completely new for everyone. People often quote the line when something happens again and again.

modersohn-verheiraten.text: I want to make good use of my single days for learning; for getting married shall be no reason for me to amount to nothing.
modersohn-verheiraten.meaning: Shortly before her wedding she says: I still want to become a real painter. Marriage should not end her career.

kafka-schwimmschule.text: Germany has declared war on Russia. – Afternoon, swimming school.
kafka-schwimmschule.meaning: The First World War begins, and in the same line Kafka writes that he is going swimming. Big world events and small everyday life stand right next to each other.

goethe-das-gute-liegt-so-nah.text: Do you always want to roam further? / Look, the good lies so near. / Just learn to seize happiness, / For happiness is always there.
goethe-das-gute-liegt-so-nah.meaning: You don't have to look for happiness far away. Often it is very close. Today people usually say: “Why roam far away? Look, the good lies so near.”

schiller-spaet-kommt-ihr.text: You come late – but you come!
schiller-spaet-kommt-ihr.meaning: You are late, but you are here, and that is good. Germans say this today in a friendly way when someone arrives late to a meeting.

ebner-freunde-nachfrage.text: There are few sincere friends – but demand is low as well.
ebner-freunde-nachfrage.meaning: A joke with words from business: Honest friends are rare, but many people don't really want honest friends either. Honesty sometimes hurts.

luther-wes-das-herz-voll.text: Out of the fullness of the heart the mouth speaks.
luther-wes-das-herz-voll.meaning: People talk a lot about what makes them very happy or very worried. Luther chose these words for the Bible because they are “good German”. Today the sentence is a proverb.

storm-weihnachtet.text: From out there in the forest I come; / I must tell you, Christmas is in the air!
storm-weihnachtet.meaning: Knecht Ruprecht comes out of the forest and brings Christmas with him. Many children in Germany learn these lines by heart during Advent.

einstein-nicht-wuerfelt.text: At any rate, I am convinced that He does not play dice.
einstein-nicht-wuerfelt.meaning: By “He” Einstein means God, whom he calls “the Old One” in the letter. He did not believe that nature is ruled by chance. The short form “God does not play dice” is well known.

busch-anders-als-man-glaubt.text: But here, as everywhere, / Things turn out other than you think.
busch-anders-als-man-glaubt.meaning: In life, something different from your plan often happens. Today Germans often say in short: “Firstly, things turn out differently, and secondly, not as you think.”

goethe-unter-palmen.text: No one walks unpunished beneath palm trees, and one's way of thinking surely changes in a land where elephants and tigers are at home.
goethe-unter-palmen.meaning: A person who lives in a foreign country for a long time changes. They think and feel differently than before. People often quote only the first part.

schiller-ernst-ist-das-leben.text: Life is serious, art is cheerful.
schiller-ernst-ist-das-leben.meaning: Life is often hard. Art, music and theatre make us lighter and happier.

nietzsche-werde-der-du-bist.text: What does your conscience say? “You shall become who you are.”
nietzsche-werde-der-du-bist.meaning: Find out what is inside you, and live by it. The idea is old and comes from the Greek poet Pindar.

kant-bestirnter-himmel.text: Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe, the more often and the longer one thinks about them: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me.
kant-bestirnter-himmel.meaning: Two things make Kant wonder again and again: the sky full of stars and the sense of good and evil in every person. The sentence is also on his memorial plaque in Kaliningrad, formerly Königsberg.

luxemburg-mensch-bleiben.text: Then see that you remain human: being human is above all the main thing.
luxemburg-mensch-bleiben.meaning: Whatever happens: the most important thing is to stay a good and warm person. Rosa Luxemburg wrote this from prison.

lichtenberg-niemals-zeit.text: The people who never have time do the least.
lichtenberg-niemals-zeit.meaning: People who always say “I have no time” are often not hard-working at all. Talking a lot about stress does not mean working a lot.

heine-wein-wasser.text: I know they drank wine in secret / And preached water in public.
heine-wein-wasser.meaning: Some people ask others to give things up, but they enjoy everything themselves. Today people say: “to preach water and drink wine”.

goethe-was-man-nicht-versteht.text: What one does not understand, one does not possess.
goethe-was-man-nicht-versteht.meaning: Learning by heart is not enough. Only when you understand something does it really belong to you.

schiller-uhr-schlaegt-keinem-glueckliche.text: The clock strikes for no one who is happy.
schiller-uhr-schlaegt-keinem-glueckliche.meaning: When you are happy, you forget the time. This is where the well-known saying “No hour strikes for the happy” comes from.

modersohn-glueck-warten.text: You just have to be able to wait; happiness will come.
modersohn-glueck-warten.meaning: Be patient. Good things often come later than you think.

kafka-heimkehr-tuer.text: The longer one hesitates in front of the door, the more of a stranger one becomes.
kafka-heimkehr-tuer.meaning: A man comes home after a long time and doesn't dare to go in. The longer you wait, the harder the first step becomes.

ebner-unuebersetzbare-worte.text: The spirit of a language reveals itself most clearly in its untranslatable words.
ebner-unuebersetzbare-worte.meaning: Every language has words that you can't translate exactly, for example “gemütlich” or “Feierabend”. These very words show how people think and feel.

luther-feste-burg.text: A mighty fortress is our God.
luther-feste-burg.meaning: God is like a strong castle that gives protection. It is one of the best-known church hymns. Note: “Ein feste Burg” is old grammar; today you say “eine feste Burg”.

hebel-frieden-ernaehrt.text: For peace nourishes, but strife consumes.
hebel-frieden-ernaehrt.meaning: When people live in peace, everyone is well. Fighting, on the other hand, costs money, strength and time. Hebel takes up an old proverb here.

goethe-was-du-ererbt.text: What you have inherited from your fathers, / Earn it, in order to possess it.
goethe-was-du-ererbt.meaning: What you get from your parents or your culture only really belongs to you when you work with it yourself and earn it anew.

schiller-pappenheimer.text: That's how I know my Pappenheimers.
schiller-pappenheimer.meaning: In Schiller it is praise for loyal soldiers. Today people usually say it ironically: “That's how these people are, I expected that.”

fontane-fremde-heimat.text: Only being abroad teaches us what we have in our homeland.
fontane-fremde-heimat.meaning: Only when we are far away do we notice what our homeland has given us. Fontane begins his big book about Brandenburg with this sentence.

storm-liebesarmen.text: Whoever has ever lived in loving arms / Can never in life grow poor.
storm-liebesarmen.meaning: Whoever was truly loved once stays rich inside, even if they have little later on.

grenzen-sprache.text: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
grenzen-sprache.meaning: What I can't say, I can't really think either. With every new word my world gets bigger.

dohm-freiheit.text: There is no freedom for men if there is no freedom for women.
dohm-freiheit.meaning: Freedom is only real if it applies to everyone. If women are not free, the whole society is not free.

morgenstern-messerscharf.text: Because, he concludes razor-sharp, / what must not be cannot be.
morgenstern-messerscharf.meaning: Palmström is hit by a car. Because cars are not allowed to drive there, he thinks: then it cannot have happened. Today people say this about people who don't want to see the facts.

goethe-schwarz-auf-weiss.text: For what you own in black and white / You can carry home with confidence.
goethe-schwarz-auf-weiss.meaning: The student wants to write everything down; then he feels safe. Today “schwarz auf weiß” (black on white) is used for something that is written on paper.

schiller-besser-als-mein-ruf.text: I am better than my reputation.
schiller-besser-als-mein-ruf.meaning: People say bad things about me, but I am a better person than that. Today people also say this with a smile about themselves.

mozart-kein-dichter.text: I cannot write poetically; I am no poet. […] But I can do it with notes; I am a musician.
mozart-kein-dichter.meaning: Mozart wants to wish his father a happy birthday. He can't do it so beautifully with words, but he can with music.

muss-muessen.meaning: No one can be forced to do anything. Every person is free.

einstein-autoritaetsdusel.text: Blind faith in authority is the greatest enemy of truth.
einstein-autoritaetsdusel.meaning: You shouldn't believe everything just because an important person says it. Whoever obeys blindly won't find the truth. Einstein was 22 years old at the time.

nestroy-fortschritt.text: In general, progress has this about it: it looks much bigger than it really is.
nestroy-fortschritt.meaning: New things often seem more important than they are. The philosopher Wittgenstein put this sentence at the beginning of his great book.

kraus-bildung.text: Education is what most people receive, many pass on, and few have.
kraus-bildung.meaning: Many people go to school and pass knowledge on. But only a few truly understand. Collecting knowledge is not the same as being educated.

goethe-vom-vater-die-statur.text: From Father I have my build, / Life's serious conduct; / From dear Mother my cheerful nature / And love of telling tales.
goethe-vom-vater-die-statur.meaning: Goethe says what he got from his parents: from his father his body and his seriousness, from his mother his good mood and his joy in telling stories.

schiller-das-alte-stuerzt.text: The old collapses, the times are changing, / And new life blossoms from the ruins.
schiller-das-alte-stuerzt.meaning: When something old comes to an end, something new and good can begin. Many people who have to start again find hope in this sentence.

rilke-leben-aendern.meaning: Rilke looks at an old statue, and it speaks to him like an order. Today people say this sentence when something touches us so deeply that we want to live differently.

claudius-wenn-jemand-eine-reise-tut.text: When someone goes on a journey, / He has a tale or two to tell.
claudius-wenn-jemand-eine-reise-tut.meaning: People who travel experience a lot and have a lot to tell afterwards. Today people usually say the line with “erzählen”, often after a holiday.

arnim-selbstdenken.text: Thinking for oneself is the highest courage. – Most people do not think for themselves.
arnim-selbstdenken.meaning: It takes a lot of courage to form your own opinion. Many people prefer to take over what others think.

schopenhauer-gesundheit.text: On the whole, though, nine tenths of our happiness rests on health alone.
schopenhauer-gesundheit.meaning: Without health you can enjoy almost nothing. The short form “Health isn't everything, but without health everything is nothing” is also well known; but that is not Schopenhauer's original text.

raimund-jugend-geld.text: Money can do much in the world, / But youth cannot be bought with money.
raimund-jugend-geld.meaning: With money you can buy a lot, but not youth. Time passes for everyone, for the rich and the poor.

goethe-schall-und-rauch.text: Feeling is everything; / A name is sound and smoke.
goethe-schall-und-rauch.meaning: For Faust, the feeling is what counts, not the word for it. Today people say “names are sound and smoke” when a name or title is not important.

schiller-drum-pruefe.text: So test, whoever binds himself forever, / Whether heart to heart is truly matched! / The madness is short, the regret is long.
schiller-drum-pruefe.meaning: Before you marry, you should check well whether you really fit together. Today people often say “So test, whoever binds himself forever” with humour, also about contracts.

droste-eine-mutter.text: Ah, a mother you only have once!
droste-eine-mutter.meaning: You have only one mother in life. In the poem, a young woman far from home gets a letter from home and cries with happiness that her mother is healthy.

marx-welt-veraendern.text: The philosophers have only interpreted the world in various ways; the point, however, is to change it.
marx-welt-veraendern.meaning: Thinking about the world is not enough. You also have to act and make things better. Today the sentence is written in the Humboldt University in Berlin.

tucholsky-seele-baumeln.text: We lay on the meadow and let our souls dangle.
tucholsky-seele-baumeln.meaning: Being completely relaxed, thinking about nothing. This gave rise to the expression “die Seele baumeln lassen” (to let your soul dangle), which people today often use for holidays.

beethoven-tugend.text: Recommend virtue to your children; it alone can make them happy, not money. I speak from experience.
beethoven-tugend.meaning: Beethoven writes to his brothers: Teach your children to be good. Money does not make you happy.

ringelnatz-kachel.text: I love you so much! / Without a second thought I'd give you / A tile from my stove / As a present.
ringelnatz-kachel.meaning: A declaration of love that is funny and touching at the same time. A strange little gift, but it comes from the heart.

goethe-weltliteratur.text: National literature doesn't mean much now; the age of world literature has arrived.
goethe-weltliteratur.meaning: Goethe means: We should not only read books from our own country. The literature of all peoples belongs together. In the same conversation he advises everyone to look around at other nations.

schiller-froemmste-nachbar.text: Even the most pious man cannot live in peace / If his wicked neighbour does not like it.
schiller-froemmste-nachbar.meaning: Even a good, quiet person gets into a fight if someone else wants a fight. People quote this when there is trouble with neighbours or between countries.

busch-musik-geraeusch.text: Music is often not found pleasing, / Because it always comes with noise.
busch-musik-geraeusch.meaning: For the musician it is art; for the neighbour it is noise. A later version is also well known: “Music is often felt to be disturbing …”

nietzsche-warum-wie.text: If one has one's own why? of life, one can put up with almost any how?
nietzsche-warum-wie.meaning: Whoever knows what they live for can bear almost any difficult situation. The sentence is often quoted freely as “He who has a why to live can bear almost any how”.

kant-erziehung.text: Man can only become man through education.
kant-erziehung.meaning: We learn almost everything from other people: language, rules, consideration for others. That's why school, parents and teachers are so important.

luxemburg-gut-sein.text: Being good is the main thing! Simply and plainly being good – that resolves and binds everything and is better than all cleverness and insisting on being right.
luxemburg-gut-sein.meaning: Being kind and good is more important than being clever or always wanting to be right.

lichtenberg-vergessen-gelesen.text: I forget most of what I have read, just like what I have eaten; but I do know this much: both nonetheless contribute to the maintenance of my mind and my body.
lichtenberg-vergessen-gelesen.meaning: You forget a lot of what you read, just as you forget yesterday's food. Still, it has nourished us. A comfort for everyone who is learning a language.

goethe-armer-tor.text: And here I stand, poor fool that I am! / And am no wiser than before.
goethe-armer-tor.meaning: Faust has studied many subjects, but he still doesn't understand the most important thing. People quote this when they have learned or searched a lot and still know nothing.

schiller-kleinste-huette.text: There is room in the smallest hut / For a happy loving pair.
schiller-kleinste-huette.meaning: When two people love each other, they don't need a big house. Today people often just say: “There is room in the smallest hut.”

heine-goettingen-wuerste.text: The town of Göttingen, famous for its sausages and its university, belongs to the King of Hanover.
heine-goettingen-wuerste.meaning: Heine makes fun of the town where he studied: he names the sausages before the university. This is how one of the funniest travel books in German begins.

modersohn-unglueck-glueck.text: Yes, that's how most people are. They write their misfortunes into their memory and diligently learn them by heart; but happiness, all that happiness, they don't notice.
modersohn-unglueck-glueck.meaning: Many people only remember the bad things. They don't see all the good in their lives.

kafka-ziel-weg.text: There is a goal, but no way; what we call the way is hesitation.
kafka-ziel-weg.meaning: We often say: I'm still on my way. Kafka means: often we are just waiting and don't dare.

ebner-jung-und-alt.text: Being young is beautiful; being old is comfortable.
ebner-jung-und-alt.meaning: Every age has something good. Young people have strength and beauty; old people no longer have to prove anything to anyone.

luther-bettler.meaning: These are Luther's last written words, shortly before his death. He means: even the wisest person has nothing of their own strength in the end. Everything we have is given to us.

goethe-nagel-auf-den-kopf.text: Many a man knocks about on the wall with a hammer and believes he hits the nail on the head every time.
goethe-nagel-auf-den-kopf.meaning: Some people talk a lot and think they are always right. “To hit the nail on the head” means: to say exactly the right thing.

hebel-gott-nicht-versuchen.text: One must not tempt God – but not people either.
hebel-gott-nicht-versuchen.meaning: You should not test or provoke anyone without need. Whoever challenges others too much will end up in trouble themselves.

fontane-einmauern.text: To shut oneself off means to wall oneself in, and to wall oneself in is death.
fontane-einmauern.meaning: Whoever cuts themselves off from other people and new ideas builds their own prison. Staying open means staying alive.

storm-graue-stadt.text: By the grey shore, by the grey sea / And off to the side lies the town.
storm-graue-stadt.meaning: Storm describes his home town Husum on the North Sea. It is grey and foggy, but he loves it anyway. To this day Husum is called “the grey town by the sea”.

wittgenstein-ehrgeiz.text: Ambition is the death of thought.
wittgenstein-ehrgeiz.meaning: Whoever only wants to win or become famous no longer thinks freely and honestly. Good thinking needs calm and curiosity.

dohm-moeglichkeiten.text: Impossibilities are the excuses of anaemic, sterile brains. Let us create possibilities!
dohm-moeglichkeiten.meaning: Whoever always says “That's not possible” is just looking for an excuse. It's better to find new ways yourself.

morgenstern-ziel-und-weg.text: Who knows not of the goal / cannot have the way, / will in the same circle / trot his whole life long.
morgenstern-ziel-und-weg.meaning: Whoever doesn't know where they want to go won't find a way either. They keep walking in circles and get nowhere.

goethe-gretchenfrage.text: Now tell me, how do you feel about religion?
goethe-gretchenfrage.meaning: Gretchen asks Faust what he believes. Today a direct, difficult question about values or faith is called a “Gretchenfrage” (Gretchen question).

mozart-denken-darf.text: … that if I am not always allowed to speak, I may at least think what I want.
mozart-denken-darf.meaning: Mozart is not always allowed to say what he thinks. But his thoughts are free, and that comforts him.

lessing-andaechtig-schwaermen.text: But do you understand / How much easier devout rapture is / Than acting well?
lessing-andaechtig-schwaermen.meaning: Beautiful, pious feelings are easy. Really doing good is much harder. Actions count more than nice words.

einstein-leidenschaftlich-neugierig.text: I have no special talent; I am only passionately curious.
einstein-leidenschaftlich-neugierig.meaning: Einstein says: it was not talent that helped him, but curiosity. Whoever asks many questions and keeps at it can learn a lot – a new language too.

nestroy-gaeste.text: If guests only knew how often they get on your nerves, nobody in the world would ever let themselves be invited again.
nestroy-gaeste.meaning: Frau von Erbsenstein says it when visitors arrive: hosts are not always happy about guests. Viennese dialect: “Gäst'” = Gäste (guests), “z'wider” = unpleasant.

kraus-hund-treu.text: No doubt, the dog is loyal. But should we therefore take him as an example? He is loyal to man, after all, and not to the dog.
kraus-hund-treu.meaning: People praise the dog for its loyalty. Kraus turns this around: the dog is not loyal to its own kind, but to its master. Is that really a model for people?

rilke-herbsttag.text: Lord: it is time. The summer was very great.
rilke-herbsttag.meaning: This is how one of the best-known German autumn poems begins. The speaker says to God: the summer was beautiful and rich; now autumn is coming.

goethe-regenbogen.text: A rainbow that lasts a quarter of an hour is no longer looked at.
goethe-regenbogen.meaning: Even the most beautiful thing becomes boring if it lasts too long. Beautiful moments are valuable because they are short.

claudius-kriegslied.text: Alas, there is war – and I desire / Not to be the one to blame!
claudius-kriegslied.meaning: There is war, and that is terrible. I do not want, in any way, to be guilty of this suffering. An early German poem against war.

arnim-wissen-liebe.text: What is knowledge that does not come from love?
arnim-wissen-liebe.meaning: Knowledge without love is cold and has little value. You learn best what you love.

schopenhauer-welt-vorstellung.meaning: Schopenhauer's main work begins with this sentence. We only know the world as it appears in our head, that is, through our eyes, ears and thoughts.

raimund-leb-wohl-stilles-haus.text: So farewell then, you quiet house, / Sadly we are moving out of you.
raimund-leb-wohl-stilles-haus.meaning: A family has to leave their house and is sad. The song became very well known in Austria. People still say the line today as a joke when they move house.

droste-heimlich-haar.text: And may only secretly loosen my hair, / And let it flutter in the wind!
droste-heimlich-haar.meaning: The poet would like to be free like a man. As a woman she has to behave well and may only show her freedom in secret.

marx-sein-bewusstsein.text: It is not the consciousness of men that determines their being, but, on the contrary, their social being that determines their consciousness.
marx-sein-bewusstsein.meaning: How we live and work shapes our thinking. In short, people often say: “Being determines consciousness.”

goethe-gluecklichen-augen.text: You happy eyes, / Whatever you have seen, / Be it as it may, / It was so beautiful!
goethe-gluecklichen-augen.meaning: The tower watchman looks back on his life. Not everything was good, but he is grateful for everything he was allowed to see.

tucholsky-fachmann.text: Don't let yourself be impressed by any expert who tells you: “My dear friend, I've been doing it this way for twenty years!” – You can do a thing wrong for twenty years, too.
tucholsky-fachmann.meaning: Long experience doesn't automatically mean something is right. You may ask experts too: Why do you do it this way?

beethoven-wahre-kunst.meaning: Real art never gets old and is never lost. People still love it after many years.

hegel-leidenschaft.text: Nothing great has been accomplished without passion, nor can it be accomplished without it.
hegel-leidenschaft.meaning: For great things you need strong feelings and enthusiasm. People who are only calm and cool rarely achieve anything special.

gellert-blinde-lahme.text: You do not have what others have, / And others lack the gifts you have; / From this imperfection / Springs our fellowship.
gellert-blinde-lahme.meaning: No one can do everything. Because everyone is good at something different, we need each other. Our very weaknesses bring us together.

ringelnatz-schenken.text: Give with wit and without guile. / Remember / That your gift / Is you yourself.
ringelnatz-schenken.meaning: A gift should be honest and not want anything back. The most important part of it is you: your time, your humour, your thoughts.

silesius-ros-ohn-warum.text: The rose is without why; it blooms because it blooms, / It pays no heed to itself, asks not whether it is seen.
silesius-ros-ohn-warum.meaning: The rose simply blooms, without a reason and without an audience. Life doesn't always need a purpose. You can do something beautiful even when nobody is watching.

goethe-mit-dem-wissen-waechst-der-zweife.text: Actually, one only knows when one knows little; with knowledge, doubt grows.
goethe-mit-dem-wissen-waechst-der-zweife.meaning: People who know little are often very sure of themselves. People who learn more see more questions and become more careful.

gotthelf-magen-seele.text: Before a meal, the thoughts of the stomach disturb the thoughts of the soul.
gotthelf-magen-seele.meaning: When you are hungry, you can't think well about big things. Eat first, then philosophise.

hofmannsthal-wiederanfangen.text: All of life is an eternal beginning again.
hofmannsthal-wiederanfangen.meaning: In life you start again and again: a new city, a new job, a new language. That is normal and not a failure.

buechner-abgrund.text: Every person is an abyss; one gets dizzy looking down.
buechner-abgrund.meaning: In every person there are dark, deep sides that we don't fully understand. If you look closely, it can make you afraid.

logau-wein-freundschaft.text: The friendship that the wine has made / Works like the wine: for just one night.
logau-wein-freundschaft.meaning: Those who quickly find friends while drinking have often lost them again by the next morning. Real friendship needs more than one evening.

raabe-beste-aerzte.text: It turned out once again that hope and joy are the best doctors.
raabe-beste-aerzte.meaning: People who hope and are happy get well faster. Good feelings often help as much as medicine.

spitteler-guete.text: And just one single virtue does my heart demand / Of every creature, the easiest: kindness.
spitteler-guete.meaning: Only one thing is asked of every living being: to be kind and good. And that is really not hard at all.

goethe-licht-und-schatten.text: Where there is much light, the shadow is deep.
goethe-licht-und-schatten.meaning: Where there is a lot of good, there is often a lot of bad too. Great people often have great faults as well. Today the sentence is a proverb.

stifter-meer.text: After the starry sky, the greatest and most beautiful thing God has created is the sea.
stifter-meer.meaning: For Stifter there is only one thing even greater and more beautiful than the sea: the sky with the stars at night.

bonhoeffer-guten-maechten.text: By kindly powers wondrously sheltered, / We wait with confidence for what may come.
bonhoeffer-guten-maechten.meaning: Bonhoeffer wrote this in the Gestapo prison shortly before Christmas. Even so, he feels protected and is not afraid of the future. Today the poem is sung as a song, often on New Year's Eve.

huch-liebe-verschwenden.text: Love is the only thing that grows when we squander it.
huch-liebe-verschwenden.meaning: Money gets less when you spend it. Love is different: the more you give, the more there is.

gerhardt-geh-aus-mein-herz.text: Go out, my heart, and seek delight / In this dear summertime / In your God's gifts.
gerhardt-geh-aus-mein-herz.meaning: Go outside and enjoy the summer, the flowers and nature. The hymn is one of the best-known German summer songs.

muehsam-niemand-frei.text: No one can be free as long as not everyone is.
muehsam-niemand-frei.meaning: Freedom is not just for me alone. As long as other people are not free, my freedom is not complete either.

moerike-er-ists.text: Spring lets its blue ribbon / Flutter through the air once more.
moerike-er-ists.meaning: Spring is coming, and you can feel it everywhere in the air. Many Germans think of these lines on the first warm days.

goethe-was-sie-laecherlich-finden.text: Nothing reveals people's character more than what they find ridiculous.
goethe-was-sie-laecherlich-finden.meaning: What someone laughs at shows what they are like. Do they laugh at weak people or at stupidity? That is how you recognise a person.

gryphius-augenblick.text: The years are not mine that time has taken from me, / The years are not mine that perhaps may come, / The moment is mine.
gryphius-augenblick.meaning: The past is over, the future is uncertain. Only the present moment really belongs to us. That's why we should use it well.

pestalozzi-verhaertung.text: The centre of all human corruption is the hardening of the heart.
pestalozzi-verhaertung.meaning: The greatest evil begins when people no longer feel compassion and their heart becomes hard.

zweig-niemand-fort.text: No one we love is gone. Love is eternal presence.
zweig-niemand-fort.meaning: A person we love stays with us, even if they are far away or have died. Love brings them to life again and again.

musil-danach-tut.text: What one does is never decisive – what counts is always what one does afterwards!
musil-danach-tut.meaning: Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is how you act afterwards and what you make of the situation.

hebbel-zauber-im-gesicht.text: Every person carries a magic in their face: someone or other likes it.
hebbel-zauber-im-gesicht.meaning: Nobody is unattractive to everyone. For someone, every face is special and beautiful.

grillparzer-eifersucht.text: Jealousy is a passion / That zealously seeks what causes pain.
grillparzer-eifersucht.meaning: A word game in German: “Eifersucht” (jealousy) = “Eifer” (zeal) + “sucht” (seeks), and “Leidenschaft” (passion) = “Leiden” (suffering) + “schafft” (creates). A jealous person always looks for reasons that make them unhappy.

goethe-mein-herz-allein.text: Ah, what I know, anyone can know – my heart is mine alone.
goethe-mein-herz-allein.meaning: You can learn and share knowledge. But your own heart, your own feelings, every person has only for themselves.

eichendorff-wuenschelrute.text: A song sleeps in all things / That go on dreaming and dreaming, / And the world begins to sing / If only you find the magic word.
eichendorff-wuenschelrute.meaning: There is something beautiful in all things. You only have to find the right word, and then it shows itself. A poem about the power of language.

trakl-winterabend.text: When the snow falls against the window, / Long the evening bell is ringing, / For many the table is laid / And the house is well provided.
trakl-winterabend.meaning: A calm picture: outside snow is falling; inside it is warm and the food is on the table. But the poem also thinks of those who are out on the road.

laskerschueler-blaues-klavier.text: At home I have a blue piano / And yet I don't know a single note.
laskerschueler-blaues-klavier.meaning: The poet lives in exile in Jerusalem. The blue piano stands for her art and for the old home she has lost.

grimmelshausen-unbestaendigkeit.text: From which it can be seen that inconstancy / Alone is constant, in joy as well as sorrow.
grimmelshausen-unbestaendigkeit.meaning: Nothing stays as it is. The only thing that always stays is change, in good times and in bad.

horvath-ganz-anders.text: You see, I'm actually quite different – I just so rarely get round to it.
horvath-ganz-anders.meaning: Many people feel that they can't show who they really are in everyday life. Today people like to quote this sentence with a smile.

chamisso-glueck-liebe.text: Happiness is love, and love is happiness, / I've said it and I won't take it back.
chamisso-glueck-liebe.meaning: A young mother holds her child and is very happy. For her, happiness and love are the same thing. Robert Schumann turned it into a song.

goethe-beste-regierung.text: Which government is the best? The one that teaches us to govern ourselves.
goethe-beste-regierung.meaning: A good government makes people independent. They learn to make good decisions themselves.

suttner-tinte.text: No sensible person would think of trying to wash out ink stains with ink, or oil stains with oil. Only blood is supposed to be washed away with blood, again and again.
suttner-tinte.meaning: Nobody cleans dirt with even more dirt. But in war, people believe they can end violence with new violence. That is not logical.

grimm-besseres-als-den-tod.text: Something better than death you can find anywhere.
grimm-besseres-als-den-tod.meaning: The donkey says this to the rooster: Come along, a better life is waiting for you somewhere. A sentence full of courage for everyone who is starting again.

hoelderlin-wo-aber-gefahr-ist.text: But where danger is, grows / The saving power also.
hoelderlin-wo-aber-gefahr-ist.meaning: Help often comes exactly in times of great need. Many people quote this sentence in hard times to give courage.

keller-lachen-geist.text: Laughing always takes a little wit. Animals don't laugh.
keller-lachen-geist.meaning: Laughing is something human. You have to understand and think in order to laugh about something.

fremde.text: The stranger is only a stranger in a strange land.
fremde.meaning: No one is a stranger everywhere. You are only a stranger in a place you don't know yet – and that changes.

novalis-immer-nach-hause.meaning: On every path we are looking for a home. For Novalis, life is a journey back to the place where we belong.

goethe-wissen-und-anwenden.text: It is not enough to know; one must also apply. It is not enough to want; one must also do.
goethe-wissen-und-anwenden.meaning: Knowledge alone doesn't help; you also have to use it. And a wish alone is not enough; you also have to act.

axt-im-haus.text: An axe in the house saves the carpenter.
axt-im-haus.meaning: If you can do repairs yourself, you don't need a tradesman. Today people say this when someone does something themselves.

busch-das-gute.text: The good – this rule is fixed and plain – / Is always the bad from which we refrain!
busch-das-gute.meaning: Here, being good just means: not doing anything bad. Busch laughs at people who think they are good just because they don't do anything wrong.

nietzsche-abgrund.text: And if you gaze long into an abyss, the abyss also gazes into you.
nietzsche-abgrund.meaning: Whoever deals with evil or darkness for a long time is changed by it. You should be careful not to become like what you are fighting.

kant-krummes-holz.text: Out of wood as crooked as that from which man is made, nothing entirely straight can be built.
kant-krummes-holz.meaning: People are never perfect. That's why you can't build a perfect society either. You should expect mistakes and be patient.

luxemburg-zu-hause.text: I feel at home in the whole world, wherever there are clouds and birds and human tears.
luxemburg-zu-hause.meaning: Her home is not a country but the whole world. Wherever there is nature and wherever people suffer, she feels at home.

anders-werden.text: I don't know whether it will get better if it changes; but this much I can say: it must change if it is to get good.
anders-werden.meaning: Change does not surely bring something good. But without change, nothing gets good.

goethe-sklave-frei.text: No one is more of a slave than the one who thinks he is free without being so.
goethe-sklave-frei.meaning: Someone who doesn't notice that he is not free cannot free himself. That's why he is the least free of all.

heine-loreley.text: I do not know what it should mean / That I am so sad.
heine-loreley.meaning: This is how the famous poem about the Lorelei on the Rhine begins. You are sad and don't know why. Many Germans know the melody by Friedrich Silcher.

modersohn-traurigsein.text: Being sad is probably something natural. It is probably a drawing of breath before joy, a preparing of the soul for it.
modersohn-traurigsein.meaning: Sadness is part of life. It is like a pause, after which joy can come again.

axt-meer.text: A book must be the axe for the frozen sea within us.
axt-meer.meaning: A good book must touch us and break open something in us that has become hard and cold.

ebner-gescheitere-gibt-nach.text: The cleverer one gives in! An immortal saying. It establishes the world domination of stupidity.
ebner-gescheitere-gibt-nach.meaning: The proverb says: the wiser one gives in. Ebner-Eschenbach means: if the clever always give in, in the end the stupid decide. Sometimes you also have to stand firm.

aufs-maul.text: You must ask the mother in the house, the children in the street, the common man at the market, and watch their mouths to see how they speak.
aufs-maul.meaning: If you want to translate well, you have to listen to how ordinary people really speak. This is where the expression “dem Volk aufs Maul schauen” (to watch the people's mouths) comes from.

hebel-bald-wieder-tag.text: I have only a little left to do, and I'll come soon, and soon it will be day again.
hebel-bald-wieder-tag.meaning: An old woman says this at the grave of her fiancé, who died 50 years ago. She hopes to see him again soon. The sentence gives courage: after the dark time, light comes again.

goethe-zauberlehrling.text: The spirits that I summoned, / I now cannot get rid of.
goethe-zauberlehrling.meaning: A sorcerer's apprentice calls up spirits, but he can't stop them anymore. Today people say “the spirits that I called” when they have started something and can no longer control it.

fontane-ribbeck.text: Herr von Ribbeck of Ribbeck in Havelland, / In his garden a pear tree stood.
fontane-ribbeck.meaning: This is how one of the most popular German poems begins. An old gentleman gives the children pears, and even after his death a pear tree grows out of his grave for them.

storm-freie-knecht.text: The one asks: What comes after? / The other asks only: Is it right? / And that is how the free man / Differs from the servant.
storm-freie-knecht.meaning: A person who is not free only thinks about the consequences for himself. A free person asks whether something is right and then acts on it.

wittgenstein-wovon-schweigen.text: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.
wittgenstein-wovon-schweigen.meaning: There are things you can't put into clear words. Then it's better to be quiet. In everyday life people also say this with a wink when someone talks about something they know nothing about.

dohm-wahres-weib.text: But – I'm supposed to be a real, a true woman! What is that, then: a true woman? To be a true woman, must I iron, sew, cook and wash little children?
dohm-wahres-weib.meaning: Dohm asks ironically: Is a woman only a “real” woman if she does housework? Her answer: No.

morgenstern-jede-sprache-schoen.text: How beautiful every – yes, every – language is when people don't just chatter in it, but actually say something.
morgenstern-jede-sprache-schoen.meaning: No language is ugly. Every language becomes beautiful when people say something real with it and don't just talk emptily.

mozart-komponiert.text: Everything is already composed – but not yet written down.
mozart-komponiert.meaning: Mozart already has the music for his opera finished in his head. He only has to write it down. Today people also say this jokingly when a piece of work is already finished in their head.

goethe-irren-und-luegen.text: When I am wrong, anyone can notice it; when I lie, not.
goethe-irren-und-luegen.meaning: Other people can see a mistake. A lie often can't be seen. That's why lying is worse than being wrong.

lessing-christ-und-jude.text: Are Christian and Jew Christian and Jew / Sooner than they are human?
lessing-christ-und-jude.meaning: First of all we are all human beings. Religion comes after that. The play is still an important text about tolerance today.

einstein-schafherde.text: To be a flawless member of a flock of sheep, one must above all be a sheep.
einstein-schafherde.meaning: Whoever always does what everyone else does doesn't think for themselves. With a joke, Einstein invites us to be brave and have our own opinion.

nestroy-das-schlechteste.text: I believe the worst of every person, even of myself, and I've seldom been wrong.
nestroy-das-schlechteste.meaning: A servant says this with black humour. If you expect the worst of everyone, you are rarely disappointed. The funny part: he doesn't leave himself out.

kraus-zeit-nicht-zu-lesen.text: Where on earth do I find all the time not to read so much?
kraus-zeit-nicht-zu-lesen.meaning: A joke about bad books and newspapers: there is so much you don't want to read that not reading is almost work.

rilke-ueberstehn.text: Who speaks of victories? Enduring is everything.
rilke-ueberstehn.meaning: Life is not always about winning. Often it is enough just to get through a hard time.

claudius-mond-ist-aufgegangen.text: The moon has risen, / The little golden stars are shining / In the sky, bright and clear.
claudius-mond-ist-aufgegangen.meaning: In the evening the moon comes out and the stars shine. The song is one of the best-known German lullabies.

goethe-edel-sei-der-mensch.text: Let man be noble, / Helpful and good!
goethe-edel-sei-der-mensch.meaning: People should be good and help others. That is what makes them something special.

arnim-sehnsucht-licht.text: What longs for light is not without light, for the longing is already light.
arnim-sehnsucht-licht.meaning: Whoever longs for something good already has something good inside. Hope itself is already a small light.

schopenhauer-schicksal.text: But what people commonly call fate is mostly just their own foolish pranks.
schopenhauer-schicksal.meaning: Many people say “bad luck” or “fate” when something goes wrong. But often they made a mistake themselves.

raimund-sonne-untergehn.text: However beautifully the sun may shine, / One day it has to set.
raimund-sonne-untergehn.meaning: Even the most beautiful time comes to an end one day. Youth sings this as it says goodbye to old Wurzel.

droste-am-meisten-fuehlt.text: Where one feels the most, one does not know much to say.
droste-am-meisten-fuehlt.meaning: When our feelings are very strong, we often can't find the words. Droste writes this in a poem for her mother.

marx-tragoedie-farce.text: Hegel remarks somewhere that all great world-historical facts and persons occur, as it were, twice. He forgot to add: the first time as tragedy, the second time as farce.
marx-tragoedie-farce.meaning: When history repeats itself, the copy is often ridiculous. People quote this today when someone badly imitates a great model.

tucholsky-mit-jemand-schweigen.text: It's lovely to be able to be silent with someone.
tucholsky-mit-jemand-schweigen.meaning: With good friends you don't always have to talk. Being quiet together and feeling comfortable is a sign of closeness.

goethe-sich-selbst-kennenlernen.text: How can one get to know oneself? Never by contemplation, but certainly by action.
goethe-sich-selbst-kennenlernen.meaning: Just thinking about yourself doesn't help much. When you do something, you notice what you can do and who you are.

beethoven-schicksal.text: I will seize fate by the throat; it shall certainly not bend me down completely – oh, it is so beautiful to live life a thousand times.
beethoven-schicksal.meaning: Beethoven is going deaf, but he doesn't want to give up. He fights against his fate because life is so beautiful.

hegel-eule-der-minerva.text: The owl of Minerva begins its flight only as dusk is falling.
hegel-eule-der-minerva.meaning: The owl is a symbol of wisdom. Hegel means: we only really understand a time when it is almost over. We often become wise only afterwards.

gellert-geniesse-entbehre.text: Enjoy what God has granted you, / Gladly do without what you don't have.
gellert-geniesse-entbehre.meaning: Be happy about what you have. And don't be sad about what you lack. That's how you become content.

ringelnatz-ameisen.text: In Hamburg there lived two ants / Who wanted to travel to Australia. / Near Altona, on the highway, / Their legs began to ache, / And so they wisely gave up / The last part of the journey.
ringelnatz-ameisen.meaning: Altona is right next to Hamburg. So the ants give up almost at once. A funny poem about big plans and little strength.

silesius-zwei-augen.text: The soul has two eyes: one looks into time, / The other turns towards eternity.
silesius-zwei-augen.meaning: People look at two things: at daily life and at what lasts forever. Both are part of us.

gotthelf-kein-wind.text: How often the mightiest powers die out, because no wind fans them!
gotthelf-kein-wind.meaning: Many people have great talent, but nobody encourages or supports them. Then their strength is lost, like a fire without air.

goethe-ueber-allen-gipfeln.text: Over all the hilltops / Is peace, / In all the treetops / You feel / Scarcely a breath; / The little birds are silent in the woods. / Just wait, soon / You too will rest.
goethe-ueber-allen-gipfeln.meaning: In the evening everything in the forest is quiet, even the birds. Soon people will be at rest too. It is one of the best-known German poems.

hofmannsthal-tiefe.text: Depth must be hidden. Where? On the surface.
hofmannsthal-tiefe.meaning: You don't have to say deep thoughts in a heavy, dark way. You can show them in simple, light words.

buechner-langeweile.text: They study out of boredom, they pray out of boredom, they fall in love, marry and multiply out of boredom, and finally die of boredom.
buechner-langeweile.meaning: The prince makes fun of people: they do everything in life only because they are bored. A bitter but witty sentence.

roth-zusammen.text: It is written that it is not good for man to be alone. So we live together.
roth-zusammen.meaning: An old man thinks about his long marriage. The love is over, but being alone is not good, and so they stay together. The sentence is sad and a little funny at the same time.

logau-rechter-dank.text: True thanks / Never grows sick, / And in its thanking / Never wavers.
logau-rechter-dank.meaning: Real gratitude doesn't stop after a short time. Whoever is truly grateful stays grateful later on too.

raabe-eigener-weg.text: Who impresses? Only the one who calmly goes his own way.
raabe-eigener-weg.meaning: People don't admire the one who is loud, but the one who calmly and surely does what he thinks is right.

spitteler-auseinanderfliehn.text: Better to part ways in harmony / Than to be together forever in quarrel and strife.
spitteler-auseinanderfliehn.meaning: It is better to separate peacefully than to stay together and always fight. This is true for friends, couples and groups.

goethe-rosen-und-aepfel.text: About roses one can write poems, / But apples you have to bite into.
goethe-rosen-und-aepfel.meaning: Poems about roses are beautiful, but apples you can eat. Practical things are sometimes more important than beautiful things.

stifter-wehen-der-luft.text: The blowing of the air, the trickling of the water, the growing of the grain, the surging of the sea, the greening of the earth, the shining of the sky, the shimmering of the stars – these I consider great.
stifter-wehen-der-luft.meaning: For Stifter, storms or wars are not great, but the quiet things that happen every day. Nature shows its strength quietly.

bonhoeffer-dummheit.text: Stupidity is a more dangerous enemy of the good than malice.
bonhoeffer-dummheit.meaning: You can defend yourself against evil people. But stupid people don't listen to arguments, and that makes them even more dangerous.

huch-abschiednehmen.text: Life is a constant saying goodbye.
huch-abschiednehmen.meaning: Every day we leave something behind: people, places, times. Huch said this at the age of 83, shortly before her death.

tmann-zwei-welten.text: I stand between two worlds, am at home in neither, and as a result I have it a little hard.
tmann-zwei-welten.meaning: Tonio feels at home neither among the artists nor among ordinary citizens. Many people who live between two countries or languages know this feeling.

gerhardt-wege-finden.text: He who gives the clouds, the air and the winds / Their ways, their course and path, / Will also find ways / Where your foot can walk.
gerhardt-wege-finden.meaning: God shows even the clouds and the wind their way. So he will also find a way for you. A hymn of comfort for hard times.

muehsam-welt-verfluchen.text: Why don't I curse the world and humanity? Because I sense the human being I am looking for.
muehsam-welt-verfluchen.meaning: Mühsam went through many terrible things. Still he doesn't hate the world, because he looks for and feels something good in every person.

goethe-pudels-kern.text: So that was the poodle's core!
goethe-pudels-kern.meaning: A poodle turns into the devil Mephisto. Today people say “des Pudels Kern” (the poodle's core) for the real, important point of a matter.

moerike-auf-eine-lampe.text: But what is beautiful seems blissful in itself.
moerike-auf-eine-lampe.meaning: Something beautiful doesn't need an audience. It is happy in itself and shines, even when no one is looking.

gryphius-heute-baut.text: What this one builds today, that one tears down tomorrow; / Where cities stand now, there will be a meadow.
gryphius-heute-baut.meaning: What one person builds today, another destroys tomorrow. Where there are cities now, grass will grow later. Gryphius wrote this during the Thirty Years' War.

pestalozzi-bruder-von-hunderten.text: Whoever, in spirit and in truth, feels like a brother to hundreds is a higher human being than the most tender brother of one.
pestalozzi-bruder-von-hunderten.meaning: It is greater to love many people like brothers and sisters than to love only one single person.

zweig-pass-heimat.text: On the day I lost my passport, I discovered at the age of fifty-eight that with one's homeland one loses more than a patch of bounded earth.
zweig-pass-heimat.meaning: In exile, Zweig loses his Austrian passport. He realises: whoever loses their homeland loses not only a piece of land, but also security and a part of themselves.

musil-moeglichkeitssinn.text: If there is a sense of reality, there must also be a sense of possibility.
musil-moeglichkeitssinn.meaning: Some people only see what is. Musil says: you also need a sense for what could be. That is how new ideas are born.

hebbel-nach-den-sternen.text: Whoever wants to travel to the stars should not look around for company.
hebbel-nach-den-sternen.meaning: If you have a very big goal, you often have to go alone. You can't wait until others come along.

goethe-tat-ist-alles.text: The deed is everything, the glory nothing.
goethe-tat-ist-alles.meaning: For the old Faust, what matters is what you really do. Whether you become famous for it doesn't matter.

grillparzer-tadeln-ist-leicht.text: Finding fault is easy, as you well know, / The deed proves it. / But there's one thing that's easier still: / It's called parroting.
grillparzer-tadeln-ist-leicht.meaning: Criticising is easy. But it's even easier to just repeat what others say without thinking for yourself.

eichendorff-mondnacht.text: It was as if the sky / Had quietly kissed the earth.
eichendorff-mondnacht.meaning: The night is so calm and beautiful, as if the sky and the earth were kissing. One of the best-known German poems about love and nature.

humboldt-ereignisse-des-lebens.text: It always seems to me that the way one takes the events of life has just as important a share in our happiness and unhappiness as those events themselves.
humboldt-ereignisse-des-lebens.meaning: Not only what happens is important, but also how we deal with it. Our attitude makes us happy or unhappy.

trakl-liebe-milde-zeit.meaning: Autumn is warm and calm, and Trakl calls it the gentle time of love. “Der Liebe milde Zeit” means: the gentle time of love.

laskerschueler-traeume.text: I weep – / my dreams fall into the world.
laskerschueler-traeume.meaning: The speaker is sad, and her hopes and wishes are being lost. A short love poem full of images.

grimmelshausen-spiegel.text: That I am a ball of changeable fortune, an example of change, and a mirror of the inconstancy of human nature.
grimmelshausen-spiegel.meaning: Simplicissimus describes himself: fortune throws him back and forth like a ball. His life shows that everything about people is always changing.

goethe-botschaft-und-glaube.text: I hear the message well, but I lack the faith.
goethe-botschaft-und-glaube.meaning: Faust hears the Easter bells, but he can no longer believe. Today people say this when they hear a piece of news but don't believe it.

horvath-aquarell-april.text: The sky is delicate, the earth pale. The world is a watercolour titled April.
horvath-aquarell-april.meaning: A spring day with light, soft colours, like a painting in watercolours. A lovely sentence if you want to describe the weather in April.

chamisso-schatten-geld.text: But you, my friend, if you want to live among people, learn to respect first the shadow, and only then money.
chamisso-schatten-geld.meaning: Peter Schlemihl sold his shadow for money and became unhappy because of it. The shadow stands for respect and belonging. Without it, money doesn't help either.

suttner-lampenfieber.text: Stage fright is a side effect of vanity, a trembling question to fate: how will I be liked?, with all the emphasis on the syllable “I”.
suttner-lampenfieber.meaning: People who are afraid before a performance think above all about themselves. Suttner says with a smile: behind the fear there is a little vanity.

grimm-wuenschen-noch-geholfen.text: In the olden days, when wishing still helped, there lived a king whose daughters were all beautiful.
grimm-wuenschen-noch-geholfen.meaning: This is how the first fairy tale of the Brothers Grimm begins. Back then, the fairy tale says, wishes still came true.

hoelderlin-versoehnung-im-streit.text: Like the quarrels of lovers are the dissonances of the world. Reconciliation is in the midst of strife, and all that is separated finds itself again.
hoelderlin-versoehnung-im-streit.meaning: Fighting is part of life, as with people who love each other. Even in a fight there is the chance to make up again.

keller-jedes-vaterland.text: Respect every man's fatherland, but love your own!
keller-jedes-vaterland.meaning: You may love your own country. But you should respect every other country and its people just as much.

goethe-blut-besondrer-saft.text: Blood is a very special juice.
goethe-blut-besondrer-saft.meaning: Faust is supposed to sign the contract with the devil in his blood. Today people say the sentence half as a joke when blood is the topic, for example when giving blood.

valentin-zukunft-beweisen.text: Whether this experiment holds significance for the future, the future will prove to us.
valentin-zukunft-beweisen.meaning: Valentin plays a scientist who talks a lot and says nothing. The sentence sounds clever but is empty: the future always shows what happens in the future.

novalis-welt-romantisiert.text: The world must be romanticised. In this way one finds the original meaning again.
novalis-welt-romantisiert.meaning: We should see the special and the wonderful in everyday life. Then life gets a deep meaning again.

meyer-genug.meaning: In the poem, Meyer celebrates autumn with its many fruits. You can never have too much of beautiful things.

freud-herr-im-eigenen-haus.text: … that the ego is not master in its own house.
freud-herr-im-eigenen-haus.meaning: We believe we decide everything inside ourselves. Freud says: a lot happens unconsciously, for example wishes and fears. Today people often say: “The ego is not master in its own house.”

uhland-alles-wenden.text: Now, poor heart, do not be afraid! / Now everything, everything must change.
uhland-alles-wenden.meaning: Spring is coming, and with it comes hope. Don't be afraid, my heart: now everything will be different and better.

sachs-schlaraffenland.text: There is a land called Cockaigne, / Well known to lazy folk, / It lies three miles beyond Christmas.
sachs-schlaraffenland.meaning: In the land of Cockaigne no one has to work; the food flies into your mouth. But it lies “beyond Christmas”, that is, nowhere. Today people say “like in Schlaraffenland” when there is a lot of everything.

goethe-grau-ist-alle-theorie.text: Grey, dear friend, is all theory, / And green the golden tree of life.
goethe-grau-ist-alle-theorie.meaning: Books and theory are dry. Real life is colourful and alive. People quote this when practice is more important than theory.

spyri-lieber-heim.text: Because I'd a thousand times rather go home to Grandfather on the mountain pasture than anything else in the world.
spyri-lieber-heim.meaning: Heidi comes back from the rich city of Frankfurt to the mountains. She says: my home is more important to me than all the money and luxury. A sentence about homesickness that many people know.

zschokke-liebe-hochachtung.text: Love and respect cannot be forced by any law; they must be earned.
zschokke-liebe-hochachtung.meaning: You can't force anyone to love or respect you. You have to earn respect and love through how you behave.

ottopeters-buergerinnen.text: For the realm of freedom I recruit women citizens!
ottopeters-buergerinnen.meaning: This was the motto of her newspaper. She wanted to win women over to becoming free citizens and having a say.

rosegger-einsame-wald.text: Only the solitary person finds the forest; where several seek it, it flees, and only the trees remain.
rosegger-einsame-wald.meaning: You only experience the peace and the mystery of the forest when you are alone. When many people come, you only see trees.

zetkin-erst-recht.text: Let us not be frightened by unfavourable outside circumstances; let us have only one answer to all difficulties: “All the more!”
zetkin-erst-recht.meaning: When things get hard, you shouldn't give up, but try even harder. People still say “Erst recht!” (all the more!) today when they carry on despite problems.

fallersleben-alle-voegel.text: All the birds are here already, / All the birds, all!
fallersleben-alle-voegel.meaning: Spring has come and the birds are back. Almost all children in Germany sing this children's song.

goethe-zwar-weiss-ich-viel.text: True, I know much, but I would like to know everything.
goethe-zwar-weiss-ich-viel.meaning: Wagner is a student and studies very hard. He already knows a lot, but he still wants to know more.

jeanpaul-dickere-briefe.text: Books are just thicker letters to friends; letters are just thinner books for the world.
jeanpaul-dickere-briefe.meaning: Whoever writes a book is talking to friends they don't know yet. And a good letter is like a small book.

feuerbach-mensch-isst.meaning: Our food makes us what we are, in the body and also in the head. Today the sentence is a proverb, and you often hear it when people talk about healthy eating.

froebel-von-kindern-lernen.text: Let us learn from our children; let us listen to the quiet reminders of their lives, to the silent demands of their hearts!
froebel-von-kindern-lernen.meaning: Adults should listen well to children. Even when children are quiet, they show what they need.

varnhagen-frage.text: What, in the end, is a human being other than a question! To ask, only to ask, to ask honestly and boldly, and to wait humbly for an answer – that is what we are here for.
varnhagen-frage.meaning: People are here to ask brave questions and to wait patiently for answers. Asking is more important than quick answers.

brant-welt-betrogen.text: The world wants to be deceived.
brant-welt-betrogen.meaning: Many people would rather believe a nice lie than the truth. People still say “The world wants to be deceived” today when others fall for tricks or advertising.

planck-nicht-mehr-irrt.text: Whoever has got so far that he no longer makes mistakes has also stopped working.
planck-nicht-mehr-irrt.meaning: Only people who do nothing anymore make no mistakes. Mistakes are part of working and learning.

goethe-zwei-seelen.text: Two souls, alas, dwell in my breast, / And one wants to break away from the other.
goethe-zwei-seelen.meaning: Faust wants two things at once that don't go together. Today people say “two souls in my breast” when they can't decide.

gauss-lernen-genuss.text: Truly, it is not knowledge but learning, not possessing but acquiring, not being there but getting there, that gives the greatest pleasure.
gauss-lernen-genuss.meaning: The best part is not the goal but the way there. Learning brings more joy than finished knowledge.

rueckert-welt-abhanden.text: I have become lost to the world, / With which I used to waste so much time.
rueckert-welt-abhanden.meaning: I have withdrawn from noisy life and am now with myself. Gustav Mahler turned it into a famous song.

simmel-heute-kommt-morgen-bleibt.text: The stranger is meant here, then, not … as the wanderer who comes today and goes tomorrow, but as the one who comes today and stays tomorrow.
simmel-heute-kommt-morgen-bleibt.meaning: Simmel describes the stranger not as a tourist, but as someone who arrives and stays. Such a person is part of the group and still brings a view from outside.

ahumboldt-zur-freiheit-bestimmt.text: All are equally destined for freedom.
ahumboldt-zur-freiheit-bestimmt.meaning: Humboldt is talking here about all the peoples of the world. No people is better than another; all people have the same right to freedom.

herder-humanitaet.text: Humanity is the character of our race; but it is only innate in us as a disposition and must really be cultivated in us.
herder-humanitaet.meaning: Humanity belongs to all of us. But we don't have it ready-made from birth. We have to learn it, through education and upbringing.

schiller-alle-menschen-brueder.text: All people become brothers / Where your gentle wing rests.
schiller-alle-menschen-brueder.meaning: Joy connects all people. Beethoven set the poem to music, and today the melody is the anthem of Europe.

goethe-zitronen-bluehn.text: Do you know the land where the lemon trees bloom?
goethe-zitronen-bluehn.meaning: The girl Mignon thinks of Italy, a warm country in the south. To this day, many Germans connect this sentence with longing for the south.

busch-sorgen-likoer.text: It is a custom from of old: / Whoever has worries also has liqueur!
busch-sorgen-likoer.meaning: Many people drink when they have problems. Busch makes a joke of it, but the story also shows: alcohol doesn't solve worries.

nicht-umbringt.text: What does not kill me makes me stronger.
nicht-umbringt.meaning: Hard times make me strong if I survive them.

kant-bequem-unmuendig.text: It is so comfortable to be immature.
kant-bequem-unmuendig.meaning: It is easy to let others think and decide for you. But Kant says: that is not good. You should think for yourself.

luxemburg-trotz-alledem.text: That is life, and that is how one must take it: bravely, undaunted and smiling – in spite of everything.
luxemburg-trotz-alledem.meaning: Life is often hard. You should still accept it bravely and with a smile.

lichtenberg-etwas-neues.text: One must do something new in order to see something new.
lichtenberg-etwas-neues.meaning: Whoever always does the same thing experiences nothing new. Try something out, and you will discover something too.

nachtgedanken.text: When I think of Germany in the night, / Then I am robbed of my sleep.
nachtgedanken.meaning: When I think of Germany at night, I can't sleep – from worry and from homesickness.

goethe-verweile-doch.text: If ever I say to the moment: / Linger a while! You are so beautiful! / Then you may cast me into chains, / Then I will gladly perish!
goethe-verweile-doch.meaning: This is Faust's bet with the devil: if he is ever completely satisfied and wants to hold on to a moment, he loses. Today people say “Linger a while, you are so beautiful” about a wonderful moment.

modersohn-schlafen.text: One simply does what one can and then goes to sleep. And that is how it happens that one day one has achieved something.
modersohn-schlafen.meaning: You don't have to fight dramatically. Whoever calmly does their work every day achieves something big in the end.

kafka-punkt-rueckkehr.text: From a certain point onward there is no more turning back. That point must be reached.
kafka-punkt-rueckkehr.meaning: Sometimes you have to go so far that you can't go back anymore. Kafka says: this is exactly the goal you should reach.

ebner-jugend-alter.text: In youth we learn; in old age we understand.
ebner-jugend-alter.meaning: Young people learn many things. What these things really mean, you often only understand much later in life.

luther-perlen-vor-die-saeue.text: You shall not cast your pearls before swine.
luther-perlen-vor-die-saeue.meaning: Don't give something valuable to people who can't appreciate it. Today people say: “That's casting pearls before swine.”

hebel-nie-mehr-scheinen.text: One must never want to seem more than one is.
hebel-nie-mehr-scheinen.meaning: Don't pretend to other people. Don't show yourself as richer, cleverer or more important than you really are.

weites-feld.meaning: That is a big, difficult topic – you can't say something about it quickly. Germans still say it like this today.

goethe-zwischen-uns-wahrheit.text: Let there be truth between us!
goethe-zwischen-uns-wahrheit.meaning: Orestes doesn't want to lie anymore. He says: the two of us should be honest with each other.

storm-tag-vergolden.text: We want to gild / The grey day, yes, gild it!
storm-tag-vergolden.meaning: Outside it is autumn, with fog and a grey sky. With friends and a glass of wine we still make the day beautiful, as if made of gold.

wittgenstein-bedeutung-gebrauch.text: The meaning of a word is its use in the language.
wittgenstein-bedeutung-gebrauch.meaning: You learn what a word means when you see how people use it. A good tip for language learning: always learn words in a sentence.

dohm-meinung.text: Certainly, everyone has the right to express his opinion freely; but the right to identify this opinion with the truth and to build pyres for those who think differently – that right he does not have.
dohm-meinung.meaning: Everyone may say their opinion. But nobody may believe that only their opinion is true and punish others for theirs.

moewen-emma.text: The seagulls all look as if their name were Emma.
moewen-emma.meaning: A nonsense sentence to make you laugh: all seagulls look the same – like ladies who all have the same name.

mozart-frau-gluecklich.text: I want to make my wife happy, and not make my fortune through her.
mozart-frau-gluecklich.meaning: Mozart doesn't want to marry for money. He wants to marry for love and make his wife happy.

lessing-verstand-verlieren.text: Whoever does not lose his mind over certain things has none to lose.
lessing-verstand-verlieren.meaning: With some terrible things, you have to get upset. Whoever stays completely calm then isn't thinking properly. “Verlieret” is an old form of “verliert” (loses).

goethe-talent-in-der-stille.text: A talent forms itself in stillness, / A character in the current of the world.
goethe-talent-in-der-stille.meaning: A talent grows when you practise quietly and alone. But your character is shaped by life with other people.

einstein-kunst-des-lehrers.text: It is the most important art of the teacher to awaken joy in creating and in understanding.
einstein-kunst-des-lehrers.meaning: A good teacher doesn't just pass on knowledge. He shows that learning and discovering are fun.

nestroy-geschwindigkeit.meaning: When something happens very quickly, that is not magic but skill. Germans still say this today when they have done something quickly.

kraus-kleine-stationen.text: The little stations are very proud that the express trains have to pass them.
kraus-kleine-stationen.meaning: About unimportant people who feel important because important people pass by them. And yet the big trains don't even stop there.

fragen-leben.text: Live the questions now. Perhaps then, gradually, without noticing it, you will one distant day live your way into the answer.
fragen-leben.meaning: You don't have to have all the answers right away. Live with your questions – the answers will come with time.

claudius-mond-halb-zu-sehen.text: Do you see the moon standing there? / Only half of it can be seen, / And yet it is round and beautiful!
claudius-mond-halb-zu-sehen.meaning: We often only see a part. Still, the whole is there and it is beautiful. You shouldn't only believe what you can see right now.

arnim-wer-liebt.text: Whoever loves learns to know; knowing teaches loving.
arnim-wer-liebt.meaning: Love makes you curious, and you learn a lot. And whoever knows a lot can love better. The two belong together.

irrt-strebt.text: Man errs as long as he strives.
irrt-strebt.meaning: Whoever wants to achieve something also makes mistakes. Mistakes are part of the way.

schopenhauer-hoeflichkeit.text: Politeness is cleverness; consequently, impoliteness is stupidity.
schopenhauer-hoeflichkeit.meaning: Being friendly makes your life easier. Being rude makes you enemies for no reason.

raimund-hobellied.text: People argue on and on / Often about the worth of happiness, / One calls the other stupid, / In the end nobody knows nothing.
raimund-hobellied.meaning: People argue about what happiness is, but nobody really knows. “Keiner weiß nix” (nobody knows nothing) is Viennese dialect; in standard German it is “keiner weiß etwas” (nobody knows anything).

droste-moor.text: Oh, it is eerie to walk across the moor / When it is swarming with heath smoke.
droste-moor.meaning: A child walks alone through the dark, foggy moor and is very afraid. Many pupils in Germany learn this poem.

marx-faehigkeiten-beduerfnisse.text: From each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs!
marx-faehigkeiten-beduerfnisse.meaning: Every person gives as much as they can and gets as much as they need. That is Marx's picture of a fair future.

tucholsky-freundschaft-heimat.meaning: With real friends you feel at home, even far away from your home country. A lovely sentence for everyone who lives in a new country.

beethoven-taub.text: Speak louder, shout, for I am deaf.
beethoven-taub.meaning: Beethoven writes that he could not say this to people. He was ashamed that a musician could no longer hear well.

goethe-himmelhoch-jauchzend.text: Rejoicing to the skies, / Grieved unto death; / Happy alone / Is the soul that loves.
goethe-himmelhoch-jauchzend.meaning: People in love are sometimes very happy and sometimes very sad. “Himmelhoch jauchzend, zu Tode betrübt” is used today for strong changes of mood.

hegel-bekannt-erkannt.text: What is familiar in general is, precisely because it is familiar, not truly known.
hegel-bekannt-erkannt.meaning: We think we understand what we see every day. But just because something is familiar to us, we haven't really thought it through yet.

gellert-lebe-wie-du.text: Live as you will wish, / When you die, to have lived.
gellert-lebe-wie-du.meaning: Imagine you are at the end of your life. How would you like to have lived then? That is how you should live already today.

ringelnatz-ueberall.text: Everywhere is wonderland. / Everywhere is life.
ringelnatz-ueberall.meaning: You don't have to travel far to find wonders. Also in everyday life, everywhere around us, there are things to be amazed at.

silesius-himmel-in-dir.text: Stop, where are you running? Heaven is within you: / If you seek God elsewhere, you will miss him forever and ever.
silesius-himmel-in-dir.meaning: Stop! You are looking for happiness far away, but it is inside you. Whoever only looks for it outside will never find it. “Fehlen” here means “to miss, not to hit”.

gotthelf-im-hause.text: What is to shine in the fatherland must begin at home.
gotthelf-im-hause.meaning: What is meant to be good for the whole country begins in the family. You first learn good values at home.

hofmannsthal-freunde.text: One has somewhat fewer friends than one assumes, but somewhat more than one knows.
hofmannsthal-freunde.meaning: Not everyone who is nice is a real friend. But some people like us without us knowing it.

goethe-der-weisheit-letzter-schluss.text: This is wisdom's final conclusion: / Only he earns freedom, as he does life, / Who must conquer it anew each day.
goethe-der-weisheit-letzter-schluss.meaning: Freedom isn't simply given to you as a present. You have to do something for it every day. Today people also say “der Weisheit letzter Schluss” (wisdom's final conclusion) ironically for a supposedly perfect solution.

buechner-so-jung.text: I am so young, and the world is so old.
buechner-so-jung.meaning: Prince Leonce feels tired and small. The world has already seen everything, and he is new in it.

roth-wohltaetigkeit.text: Charity satisfies first and foremost the benefactors.
roth-wohltaetigkeit.meaning: People who donate or help often feel good themselves afterwards. Roth asks critically who benefits most from the help.
